doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

chapter: Discovering jazz and the trad band
title: National service in the cavalry
summary: Denied deferment, he served two years doing clerical work in the tank corps, practised alone, and found the band had lost ground.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: You said you were the interval band, the relief band, is that what they called you?
Yeah. But our name was on the poster, our name was on the tickets, you know, we were going to really do it. So there you are.
Oh man. Couldn’t get a deferment?
Nope. They weren’t prepared to listen to any of that.
What did you end up doing in the military?
I went and served in the Cavalry, that’s the tank corps in England and in Germany, but I did basically clerical jobs, in what we called the Order Room, which is the headquarters.
Okay so you get out of the service and you were what, in your late 20s?

No, I was about 21 I suppose. We just did two years national service you see. I bought my trombone with me everywhere. I never found any other people that wanted to play, but I played, all on my own. A bit pathetic. Re-formed the band when we came out. It wasn’t quite the same again. And by that time, with two years gone, we’d lost ground.
